first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and memory_86 directly demonstrated that shortening onboarding improves completion rates and time-to-value. Memory_31 showed signup simplification drives SMB activation. Both are directly relevant to the current performance decline. Simplifying onboarding avoids the retention risk flagged in memory_73 (promotional pricing harmed 30-day retention) and is orthogonal to competitive pricing pressure. This is a proven lever for self-serve adoption that addresses both visible metrics. Referral incentives (memory_57) and activation messaging (memory_91) are secondary options, but onboarding addresses the root metric decline directly. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is valuable but doesn't address the self-serve activation/completion problem driving the QoQ drop. A standard experiment tests whether the previous lift from onboarding simplification persists or whether baseline conditions have shifted.

final.rationale: Archive confirms memory_86: onboarding simplification delivered +13% completion, -2.1 days time-to-value, and +3% retention lift. Archive confirms memory_31: signup simplification lifted SMB activation +9% with +4% qualified revenue and only -1% retention risk (acceptable). Current situation shows completion down 4% QoQ and activation down 6% QoQ. Both headwinds align directly with what these interventions addressed. The verified data shows onboarding simplification produces durable gains across completion, speed, and retention—no material downstream risk. This is a proven, low-risk lever that addresses the visible metric declines without the retention harm of promotional pricing (memory_73) or the segment specificity questions around other options. Standard experiment scope is appropriate given we have baseline confidence in the mechanism, but real-world conditions may have shifted.
